text: The United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has filed an annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020, pursuant to Section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The registrant, AMCOR PLC, is incorporated in Jersey and has the IRS Employer Identification Number 98-1455367. Its principal executive offices are located at 83 Tower Road North, Warmley, Bristol, United Kingdom BS30 8XP, and its telephone number is +44 117 9753200. The company’s ordinary shares, par value $0.01 per share, are traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol AMCR, and its 1.125% Guaranteed Senior Notes Due 2027 are traded under the symbol AUKF/27 on the same exchange. There are no securities registered under Section 12(g) of the Act. AMCOR is classified as a well-known seasoned issuer and is not required to file reports under Section 13 or 15(d) of the Act. The registrant has filed all required reports during the preceding 12 months and has been subject to such filing requirements for the past 90 days. It has also submitted electronically all Interactive Data Files required under Rule 405 of Regulation S-T. AMCOR is categorized as a large accelerated filer. The registrant has filed a report on and received an attestation to its management’s assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting under Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. AMCOR is not a shell company. The aggregate market value of its ordinary shares held by non-affiliates, calculated using the closing price on the last business day of the most recently completed second quarter, was $17.4 billion. As of August 25, 2020, the company had 1,568,481,519 shares issued and outstanding. Certain information in Part III of the report is incorporated by reference from the Amcor plc definitive Proxy Statement for its 2020 Annual Shareholder Meeting, which will be filed with the SEC within 120 days of the fiscal year end. The report includes a table of contents and covers sections such as Business, Risk Factors, Properties, Legal Proceedings, Market for Common Equity, Selected Financial Data, Management’s Discussion and Analysis, Financial Statements, and Controls and Procedures. The document also contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties, including the financial and operational impacts of the 2019 Novel Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, changes in consumer demand, loss of key customers, significant competition, integration challenges of acquisitions, difficulties in expanding through organic growth or acquisitions, threats to intellectual property, global economic conditions, international operations, raw material and energy price fluctuations, supply and commercial risks, and counterparty credit risks.

Factors that could cause actual results to differ from expectations include the continued financial and operational impacts of the 2019 Novel Coronavirus ("COVID-19") pandemic on Amcor and its customers, suppliers, employees, and the geographic markets in which they operate (see Part II, "Item 1A. - Risk Factors" for more information about the risks to the Company due to COVID-19); changes in consumer demand patterns and customer requirements across numerous industries; the loss of key customers, a reduction in their production requirements, or consolidation among key customers; significant competition in the industries and regions where the Company operates; failure to successfully integrate acquisitions within the expected time frame; inability to expand the business effectively through organic growth, including product innovation, or through acquisitions; challenges to or loss of intellectual property rights; challenging global economic conditions; the impact of operating internationally; price fluctuations or shortages in the availability of raw materials, energy, and other inputs, which could adversely affect the business; production, supply, and other commercial risks, including counterparty credit risks, which may be exacerbated during economic downturns; failure in information technology systems; inability to attract and retain key personnel; costs and liabilities related to current and future environmental, health, and safety laws and regulations; labor disputes; the possibility that the phase-out of the London Interbank Offered Rate ("LIBOR") causes interest expense to increase; foreign exchange rate risk; an increase in interest rates; a downgrade in the Company’s credit rating, which could increase borrowing costs and negatively affect financial condition and results of operations; failure to hedge effectively against adverse fluctuations in interest rates and foreign exchange rates; a significant write-down of goodwill and/or other intangible assets; the need to maintain an effective system of internal control over financial reporting; inability of insurance policies, including those provided through a captive insurance company, to offer adequate protection against all risks; litigation or regulatory developments; changing government regulations in environmental, health, and safety matters; and the ability to develop and successfully introduce new products and to develop, acquire, and retain intellectual property rights. Additional factors are discussed in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including in the sections entitled "Item 1A - Risk Factors" and "Item 7 - Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," and in Amcor’s subsequent filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Forward-looking statements in this Annual Report on Form 10-K relate only to events as of the date the statements are made. Amcor assumes no obligation and disclaims any obligation to update the information contained in this report. All forward-looking statements in this Annual Report on Form 10-K are qualified in their entirety by this cautionary statement.  

Amcor plc (ARBN 630 385 278) is a holding company originally incorporated under the name Arctic Jersey Limited as a limited company under the Laws of the Bailiwick of Jersey in July 2018, to effect the Company’s combination with Bemis Company, Inc. On October 10, 2018, Arctic Jersey Limited was renamed "Amcor plc" and became a public limited company incorporated under the Laws of the Bailiwick of Jersey. On June 11, 2019, the Company completed the acquisition of Bemis Company, Inc. ("Bemis"), a global manufacturer of flexible packaging products, pursuant to the definitive merger agreement (the "Agreement") between Amcor Limited and Bemis dated August 6, 2018. Under the terms of the Agreement, Bemis shareholders received 5.1 Amcor shares for each share of Bemis stock and Amcor shareholders received one Amcor CHESS Depositary Instrument ("CDI") for each share of Amcor Limited stock issued and outstanding. Upon completion of the transaction, the Amcor shares were registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") and traded on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") under the symbol "AMCR," and the CDIs representing the Company’s shares on the Australian Securities Exchange ("ASX") are traded under the symbol "AMC." In addition, Amcor Limited shares were delisted from the ASX and Bemis shares were delisted from the NYSE.  

The Company’s business strategy consists of three components: a focused portfolio, differentiated capabilities, and the aspiration to be THE leading global packaging company. To fulfill this aspiration, the Company is determined to win for its customers, employees, shareholders, and the environment. The focused portfolio includes businesses with a focus on primary packaging for fast-moving consumer goods, good industry structure, attractive relative growth, and multiple paths to win through leadership position, scale, and other competitive advantages. These criteria have led to the current portfolio of strong businesses across flexible and rigid packaging, specialty cartons, and closures. Our products have historically been and continue to be highly competitive, with key areas of competition including service, innovation, quality, and price. Competitors include AptarGroup, Inc., Ball Corporation, Berry Global Group, Inc., CCL Industries Inc., Crown Holdings, Inc., Graphic Packaging Holding Company, Huhtamaki Oyj, International Paper Company, Mayr-Melnhof Karton AG, O-I Glass, Inc., Sealed Air Corporation, Silgan Holdings Inc., Sonoco Products Company, WestRock Company, and various privately held companies. We consider ourselves a significant participant in the markets we serve, though due to the diversity of our business, our exact competitive position in these markets is not reasonably determinable. Working capital fluctuates annually based on business volume and market conditions, and we maintain inventory levels that balance favorable raw material procurement with the ability to fulfill customer orders promptly. Manufacturing backlogs are not a significant factor in our operating industries. Major raw materials include polymer resins and films, paper, inks, adhesives, aluminum, and chemicals, all sourced from various global suppliers, with no significant dependence on any single supplier. While temporary industry-wide shortages may occur, we expect to manage raw material supplies without significant interruptions; currently, raw materials are readily available, though pricing may vary. We own or license numerous U.S. and international patents, patent applications, trademarks, and maintain certain technologies and processes as trade secrets, which collectively provide a competitive advantage. However, the loss of any single patent or license would not have a material adverse effect on our overall results of operations or reporting segments. Patents, patent applications, and license agreements will expire or terminate over time as required by law or their terms. Amcor believes responsible packaging is essential, as it protects and preserves food and healthcare products, reduces carbon footprint and waste, extends shelf life, and minimizes product loss across distribution channels. Consumers prefer cost-effective, convenient, and easy-to-use packaging with end-of-life solutions to reduce waste. In January 2018, Amcor became the first global packaging company to commit to making all of its packaging recyclable or reusable by 2025, increasing the use of recycled materials, and collaborating globally to improve packaging recycling. We are recognized for our innovation, holding thousands of active patents, and work with customers, suppliers, and innovators to develop industry-leading solutions and support waste collection, sorting, and recycling infrastructure while educating consumers on environmental impacts. We are uniquely positioned to lead in sustainable and environmentally friendly packaging, which represents a key growth opportunity. Our operations and owned or leased real property are subject to broad environmental laws and regulations across multiple jurisdictions, covering emissions, waste handling, contamination cleanup, and environmental protection. We believe we are in substantial compliance with these regulations through our Environmental, Health, and Safety Management System and regular audits, though we cannot predict with certainty whether future liabilities for noncompliance—due to contamination at former or current sites (including from prior owners or operators) or off-site disposal of regulated materials—could arise, and such liabilities could be material. Additionally, environmental regulations are constantly evolving, and we cannot always anticipate changes. Our relations with employees under these agreements remain satisfactory, and there have been no significant work stoppages or labor disputes in the past three years. The business operations of each reporting segment are not materially seasonal. The following factors, along with other risks described in this Annual Report on Form 10-K or in other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, could negatively affect the Company’s consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows. Other unknown factors not currently known to the Company or believed to be immaterial could also impact its business and financial performance. Strategic risks include changes in consumer demand, where shifts in preferences—driven by cost, convenience, health, environmental, or social concerns—could reduce demand for certain products or render existing products obsolete, even though the Company has implemented strategies to mitigate such declines; however, these strategies are not guaranteed to succeed, and new products may fail to meet sales or margin expectations due to inaccurate demand forecasting, changing end-user preferences, or delays in development. Changes in packaging formats may increase demand for other products, but if not offset by demand for new or alternative products, consumer preference shifts could harm the Company’s business, cash flow, financial condition, and operations. Key customer concentration poses a significant risk, as the loss of major customers, a reduction in their production needs, or consolidation among key customers could severely impact sales and profitability. A single customer may at times account for 10% or more of revenue, with sales to the largest customer representing approximately 11% of total net sales in fiscal years 2019 and 2018; no single customer exceeded 10% of net sales in 2020 or any other period. Customer concentration is especially pronounced in certain business units, and adverse changes in supply agreements or customer decisions—such as switching to competitors, adopting alternative packaging, manufacturing in-house, or renegotiating terms on less favorable conditions—could materially harm the Company. Additionally, customer consolidations, such as acquisitions of companies with similar or complementary product lines, have increased business concentration and may lead to pricing pressure, potentially reducing margins. While the Company has generally managed these consolidations successfully, increased pricing pressure could materially affect operations. Competition remains significant across geographies and end-use areas, with varying entry barriers and competitive behaviors; the Company regularly bids for business and adapts to consumer demand, but cannot predict future competitive shifts. Competitors may introduce disruptive technologies or innovations that could undermine the Company’s ability to retain or acquire customers, negatively impacting its plans and financial results. The Company aims to expand through organic growth, including product innovation and customer expansion in emerging markets, and through acquisitions. However, organic growth may be limited by market saturation or reduced customer growth due to economic or strategic changes, and product innovation failures could hinder growth and competitive positioning. Over the past decade, the Company has pursued growth via acquisitions, including the 2019 acquisition of Bemis. There is no assurance that suitable acquisition targets will be identified in the right regions or with appropriate strategies, or that such acquisitions can be completed on acceptable terms. Competitors are also pursuing similar strategies, increasing competition for targets, and the current low-interest-rate environment has raised acquisition price multiples above historical averages. If the Company cannot identify suitable targets or close deals on acceptable terms, acquisition-driven growth may be restricted, negatively affecting strategic goals and expected financial benefits. Integration of acquisitions presents challenges, including difficulties in merging business processes, systems, and cultures, and potential disruptions to normal operations. The Company expects cost synergies from acquisitions, such as approximately $180 million in estimated pre-tax annual net cost savings from procurement, manufacturing, and general and administrative efficiencies from the Bemis acquisition by the end of the third year post-acquisition. While the Company is currently on track to achieve these Bemis synergies, there is no certainty that full savings will be realized or sustained. Failure to successfully integrate acquisitions or achieve expected synergy benefits could result in delayed or incomplete realization of benefits, or increased costs. Intellectual property risks include potential challenges or loss of rights, which could impair competitive ability. The Company holds patents, trademarks, trade names, and licenses related to its products, methods of use, and manufacturing, and relies on trade secrets and know-how. It protects intellectual property through legal frameworks and non-disclosure agreements. However, third parties could obtain information without authorization, independently develop similar technologies, or breach agreements. Many emerging markets lack robust intellectual property protections compared to developed jurisdictions like the United States and the European Union, increasing the risk of unauthorized use, which could reduce competitive advantages, lead to lost sales, or harm the business. Although the Company has not received significant claims of infringement, there is no assurance that such claims will not arise in the future, and the costs of protecting intellectual property could negatively affect operations.
